subject: Daggerford market square
fact: The market square contains a bronze-cast forearm mounted on a stone pillar, a smaller inscription on the back, and a secondary Dwarven inscription on the base.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. ... Then Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. ... There was a smaller inscription on the back.

subject: bronze-cast forearm
fact: The bronze-cast forearm is severed at the elbow and mounted on a stone pillar in Daggerford's market square.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar.

subject: Dwarven inscription
fact: The Dwarven inscription on the base of the monument reads 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: *The move is yours.*

subject: smaller inscription
fact: The smaller inscription on the back of the monument is in Common and reads 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.'
source_quote: *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.*

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin who died in Daggerford three years ago while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was active in Daggerford and was broken up by Tarvis Ulain.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Tarvis Ulain served Bahamut, as confirmed by the inscription on the monument.
source_quote: confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud is referenced as the figure associated with the chess-related inscription 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher and signed the monument's inscription as a witness for the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet commissioned the monument to Tarvis Ulain and recorded its creation.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where Thorin and the party eventually arrived after viewing the monument.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Pewter hand casts, miniature reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed arm, are being sold by a village priest at the River Shining Tavern.
source_quote: carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: village priest
fact: A village priest sells pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s arm at the River Shining Tavern for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast...

subject: Maerith
fact: Maerith is the mother of Elin, a seven-year-old girl who has been silent for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away. ... My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin, a seven-year-old girl, has not spoken for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: six-pointed star
fact: Elin draws the same six-pointed star on every flat surface in her home.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: lesser restoration on Elin
fact: Dawnbringer casts lesser restoration on Elin, allowing her to speak one sentence.
source_quote: Lesser restoration settled in. And then she spoke.

subject: Elin's utterance
fact: Elin says, 'The wells are not wells anymore,' after being restored by Dawnbringer.
source_quote: "The wells are not wells anymore."

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Grygum associates Elin’s condition with Zuggtmoy, a deity of fungi, and considers fungal infection as a possible cause.
source_quote: I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identifies the mechanism of Elin’s condition as distorted audio input from the Underdark.
source_quote: Zalthir articulated the mechanism: the input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has been experiencing pressure in his head for some time, which Grygum links to Elin’s condition.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named after a wizard who was burned alive by a dragon cult decades ago.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued. A wizard, burned alive, dragon cult, decades prior.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The south wall of The Burning Wizard Inn bears the spot where the wizard was burned alive, and it has never been painted over.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper ... pointed to the south wall without prompting ... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall.'

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum is the gnome innkeeper of The Burning Wizard Inn, who has lived there for thirty years and remembers the story of the burned wizard.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper, old enough to have heard the story from the people who told it first

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels.
source_quote: Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a window behind the performer’s corner that is narrow but usable in an emergency.
source_quote: The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: traveling bard
fact: A traveling bard performs at The Burning Wizard Inn with a drum and sings 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'
source_quote: There was a bard — a traveling one, by the look of her kit, set up in the performer's corner with a drum and a competent audience. She had a closing number she'd been doing all season. This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'

subject: performance of 'The Kenku Could Not Fly'
fact: The traveling bard performs 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' with the chorus: 'Oh, the Kenku could not fly, but he flew in his black hood, in his black hood, in his black hood.'
source_quote: "Oh, the Kenku could not fly, but he flew in his black hood, in his black hood, in his black hood. The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed, said the small, wise man at his side."

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler is a Kenku thief from an earlier age who, according to the song, took only what was necessary from Tiamat’s hoard.
source_quote: The Kenku thief of some earlier age who, presented with the complete hoard of Tiamat, had apparently taken only what was necessary for legitimate expenses.

subject: Tiamat
fact: Tiamat’s hoard is referenced in the bard’s song as the object from which Whistler took only what was needed.
source_quote: presented with the complete hoard of Tiamat

subject: Underdark corruption spreading to the surface
fact: Something from the Underdark is bleeding upward, affecting perception and causing voices and hallucinations on the surface.
source_quote: something from below was bleeding up, ... the madness from the Underdark ... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: connection between Elin and Daz
fact: Grygum suspects a tenuous connection between Elin’s condition and Daz’s head pressure, suggesting a shared origin.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite inscription appears on a monument dedicated to a Bahamutian paladin, despite religious differences.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer intervenes to cast lesser restoration on Elin without invitation.
source_quote: Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation. The sword has opinions about when to make an entrance, and this was apparently an occasion. 'Let me bring the light to you.'
